ai.description: Nanorana annandalii is a medium-sized frog (40–60 mm) with a brown, warty dorsum and pale belly. It is distinguished by a distinct tympanum and robust, muscular limbs adapted for high-altitude streams.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nanorana annandalii* is best distinguished by the presence of prominent, black-tipped nuptial spines on the chest and forelimbs of males, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: Nanorana annandalii inhabits high-altitude streams and marshy areas within Himalayan moist temperate forests, typically at elevations ranging from 2,000 to 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Annandale's Paa Frog is primarily nocturnal, often found hiding under rocks in fast-flowing mountain streams during the day to avoid predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nanorana annandalii* breeds in mountain streams during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of pigmented eggs attached to submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nanorana annandalii* is endemic to the Eastern Himalayas, specifically found in West Bengal and Sikkim at elevations between 1,500 and 3,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Nanorana annandalii* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes emitted by males from within fast-flowing mountain streams.
